hypothesis: The N=128 force deficit (m2 fixed at 0.5, data_seed 0, e in [0, 0.5], 4 layers, d_model=64) exists partly because context_len=128 covers only one orbit at N=128 but two orbits at N=64. If N=128 is given context_len=256, so that it also sees two orbits, its 6000-step trained force R2 at layer 1 rises at least 0.04 above the context_len-128 N=128 reference for the same seed, and closes to within 0.04 of the same seed's N=64 6000-step value. References for seed 23: N=128 0.69583 at layer 1 (run-20261014-021335-eb64) and N=64 0.7684 at layer 1 (run-20261014-031344-6b2c). References for seed 22: N=128 0.68077 at layer 4, so its layer-1 comparison is cross-layer and flagged (run-20261014-021335-4030), and N=64 0.8235 at layer 1 (run-20261014-031344-3f3d). Scoring is at fixed layer 1 from probes_final, unrounded. The best-margin layer and layer 4 are reported as secondary. Trained R2 is compared, not margin. All reference run IDs are cited. accel_step is described only, not scored.
expected_if_true: In both seeds, layer-1 trained force R2 is >= 0.736 (seed 23) and >= 0.721 (seed 22, cross-layer reference), and is within 0.04 of the same seed's N=64 value (>= 0.728 for seed 23, >= 0.783 for seed 22). Force beats its control. accel_step still beats its control.
expected_if_false: In both seeds, layer-1 trained force R2 is within 0.02 of the context_len-128 N=128 reference (<= 0.716 for seed 23, <= 0.701 for seed 22), so context length does not explain the deficit. A split between seeds, or values that fall between these bands, is inconclusive.
